newsitem.title: USA: Ohio soybean planting edges ahead of normal pace.
newsitem.headline: Ohio soybean planting edges ahead of normal pace.

text.p: Soybean seedings in Ohio edged ahead of the average pace last week amid mostly favorable planting weather, according to the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.
"There was a sign of relief as the growers took full advantage of the weather by increasing their planting, haying and harvesting progress," the report said.
Eighty-eight percent of soybeans had been planted as of Sunday, up from 56 percent last year and a five-year average of 86 percent.
Soybean emergence had reached 69 percent, still slightly behind the average pace of 71 percent.

"The low-lying ponding areas are starting to recede and some growers are still debating whether or not to replant. Some of the crops in water-saturated areas are looking better than anticipated," the report said.
Corn emergence had reached 95 percent, ahead of the average pace of 89 percent. Corn was rated 53 percent good to excellent, down slightly from 56 percent a week earlier.
Winter wheat was 86 percent headed, down from a five-year average of 95 percent. It was rated 56 percent good to excellent, down from 58 percent a week earlier.
